title: Landfill Airspace Recovery Contractor
one_liner: Mine old landfill cells to recover airspace, not metals, and sell it to operators at a fraction of the cost of new capacity.
customer: Owners of landfills with under about 10 years of permitted capacity, in airspace-constrained markets: municipal and regional authorities, and independents in the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and parts of the West.
problem: New landfill cells take years to permit and tipping fees in constrained markets often exceed $100 per ton. Insiders dismiss landfill mining because recovered metals and RDF are low value, so nobody prices the airspace.
solution: An airspace audit (drone LiDAR, borings, waste characterization) followed by a mobile trommel and ballistic-separator spread. It excavates old cells, screens fines for cover and fill, pulls metals and plastics, and re-places compacted residual. Contracts are priced per cubic yard of airspace recovered, compared to the cost of new capacity and haul-out. It skips cells with unknown PFAS risk until sampled.
why_now: Elevated commodity prices, cheaper vision sorting and robotics, tighter EPR and diversion rules that shrink incoming tonnage certainty, and PFAS liability pushing operators to characterize legacy cells anyway.
revenue_model: $25-75K audit fee, then $/CY of airspace recovered (or a share of avoided haul-out cost), plus a share of recovered commodities.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone prices the contents of the landfill. The scarce, regulated, appreciating asset is the airspace, and the true replacement lead time is 10 years.
first_30_days: Screen 20 landfills with under 7 years of remaining capacity using public permit data and satellite volumetrics. Offer free desktop screening and a paid audit of the oldest cell. Lease a trommel by the month rather than buying.

title: Refundable Deposits Against AI Submission Floods
one_liner: A gateway that makes AI-generated reports, applications and pitches post a small refundable stake, so maintainers only read submissions someone bet on.
customer: Open-source maintainers and foundations, bug-bounty program owners, and other inboxes overwhelmed by AI-generated submissions (journals, grant makers, VC and press inboxes, public-comment portals). Start with OSS security teams and mid-size bounty programs.
problem: curl scrapped its bug bounty in January 2026 after valid reports fell below 5%, and its maintainer floated an entrance fee. HackerOne reportedly paused its Internet Bug Bounty in March after a 76% year-on-year jump in submissions, and other projects have retired bounties. Agents removed the effort-based backpressure open-source governance relied on. Content classifiers lose the arms race to models that write plausible reports.
solution: A stake API and form: the submitter (human or agent) posts a refundable deposit of $5-$50 by card or machine payment. Triage marks the report valid (refund plus any bounty) or invalid (deposit goes to maintainers or charity). Integrations for GitHub Security Advisories, email intake and bounty-platform webhooks. Reporters with track records get deposit discounts, and unpaid stakes flow to the program.
why_now: The curl and HackerOne events are recent and public. Machine Payments Protocol (March 2026) and card rails make small, programmatic deposits practical, and agents now file at scale.
revenue_model: 10-15% of forfeited deposits plus $99-$499/month per program for triage tooling, with sponsor-funded tiers for open-source projects.
non_obvious_insight: Price is the only filter that scales with attacker capacity. An agent must risk money on every claim, honest reporters get refunded, so the cost lands only on slop. Postage as a spam filter failed when senders were humans, but agent-operated senders have budgets and ROI math.
first_30_days: Build a GitHub Security Advisory plus web-form integration in two weeks. Recruit 5 OSS projects that have publicly complained and run a 30-day pilot measuring valid-report rate. Then approach bounty platforms with the data.

title: Recovery Audits for Downstream Tariff Refunds
one_liner: A contingency-fee recovery-audit firm that mines buyers' AP invoice history for IEEPA-era price step-ups and files contract claims against suppliers who pocketed the tariff refund.
customer: Mid-market companies that paid tariff-inflated prices but were not importer of record: hospital systems and GPOs, restaurant groups, distributors, contractors, regional retailers. They pay 20-30% of dollars recovered. Secondary buyers: importers who want a defensible refund-sharing allocation, and plaintiffs' firms that need per-customer surcharge damages.
problem: Importers stand to receive roughly $166B of IEEPA refunds. Downstream buyers who paid blended, un-itemized price increases have no easy way to size or claim their share. A commercial litigator quoted by CFO.com says his team reads hundreds of thousands of invoices by hand to compare pre-tariff and tariff-period pricing, and that many suppliers keep the refund unless asked. In parallel, at least 25 customer suits (Amazon, Costco, Walmart, Sony and others) plead unjust enrichment. Plaintiffs will need per-customer surcharge data that nobody has assembled.
solution: Ingest a buyer's AP/ERP invoice line-item export (or PDFs via extraction). Normalize SKUs and suppliers. Detect step-changes in unit price against control SKUs and commodity indices around the tariff effective dates. Infer country of origin and HTS duty exposure from public tariff tables. Estimate the IEEPA-attributable overcharge per supplier. Then generate claim packets keyed to each contract's price-adjustment, cost-pass-through or MFN clauses, with demand-letter templates and a supplier-response tracker. Start with contracts that have explicit surcharge or cost-plus language, where recovery is strongest. Partner with one or two commercial litigation boutiques for enforcement, and have human analysts review the top claims. Second product: a refund-allocation ledger for importers and distributors that want to share refunds with customers, as Williams-Sonoma and O'Reilly are doing. Third product: a damages engine for class counsel.
why_now: The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs in February 2026. CBP's CAPE refund portal opened April 20, 2026. CBP had paid $100B by August 7, and CAPE Phase 3 for finally liquidated entries starts October 6, 2026. An Atlanta Fed survey (September 24) says most companies will hold refunds as cash. A trade court also ruled the 10% global tariff illegal on May 7, so more refund waves may follow. Contract-notice and limitation windows are running now.
revenue_model: 20-30% contingency on recovered dollars. Flat $15-50k fee for importer-side allocation reports. Per-matter fees from plaintiffs' firms. Possible later add-on: an expected-value model for funds that buy refund claims.
non_obvious_insight: For downstream buyers the refund is not a customs-law problem. It is an AP-data forensics problem, the same shape as classic recovery audits (freight, telecom, sales tax), which are paid on contingency, and the recovery-audit firms have not pivoted to it. The evidence shows the gap is manual labor: CFO.com describes lawyers examining 'hundreds of thousands of invoices' to find blended tariff pricing (https://www.cfo.com/news/these-businesses-didnt-pay-tariffs-theyre-seeking-refunds-anyway-Glen-Frost-Tim-Meyer/823107/). At least 25 customer suits need per-customer surcharge data (https://www.cfodive.com/news/amazon-companies-fighting-centralized-tariff-refund-suits-costco-cfo/830814/). Refund claims are also being sold at steep discounts (American Eagle sold $68.9M of claims for $18.6M), which shows the claims are being priced without data (https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/retailers-eager-for-cash-sell-off-rights-to-potential-tariff-refunds/827064/). CBP paid $100B by August 7 (https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/cbp-has-paid-100b-in-ieepa-tariff-refunds/827257/). Main risk: B2B pass-through litigation is largely untested, so lead with contract-backed claims.
first_30_days: Pick 3 verticals with blended pricing and heavy AP volume (medical/dental supply buyers, restaurant groups, HVAC/plumbing contractors, regional grocers). Offer a free 'tariff exposure scan' from 12 months of AP export and run it on 3-5 pilot datasets. Sign a contingency engagement with a trade or commercial litigation boutique for enforcement. Build supplier claim-packet templates for the 10 most common contract clause types. Aim for the first demand letters in week 4 and first recovered dollars inside 90 days.

title: Landed-Cost Lock for Crowdfunding Creators
one_liner: A per-campaign engine that decides what each pledge tier really costs to land in each country (HTS class, duties, freight, platform and pledge-manager fees) and configures the tariff surcharge and shipping table before a creator commits.
customer: Kickstarter and Indiegogo creators in tabletop games and hardware who have raised or plan to raise $50K-$2M, especially China-manufactured products shipping to US backers. Payer is the creator, or the small publisher's ops lead.
problem: The de minimis exemption ended May 2, 2025, so every backer parcel from China is now dutiable. Kickstarter's Tariff Manager only collects a surcharge at pledge-manager checkout (US addresses only); it does not tell the creator what number to charge. Creators end up guessing, and publishers have shut or laid off staff over the resulting margin hits.
solution: A lightweight web tool plus human-reviewed audit. The creator uploads BOM, carton dimensions, weights and destination mix. The tool returns an HTS classification with duty scenarios (DDP vs DAP), a costed shipping table by country, a 20-30% contingency, net-of-fees margin by tier (platform fee plus payment fee of roughly 8-10%, plus the BackerKit or Gamefound fee), and the exact surcharge and copy for the backer update. It adds an address-validation and duty pre-flight on the pledge-manager export.
why_now: US tariff and de minimis rule changes in 2025 are still moving through 2026, and Kickstarter launched Tariff Manager as a collection-only feature. Freight remains volatile. Creators now need a decision layer, not a checkout field, and the incumbents in this space are fulfillment companies whose content is marketing rather than tools.
revenue_model: $750-$2,500 flat fee per campaign audit (pre-launch or mid-campaign), $99/mo post-campaign ship-readiness subscription (address validation, duty pre-flight, surcharge reconciliation), and 0.25% of surcharges collected via the tool as an optional success fee.
non_obvious_insight: The platform solved collection but not decision-making. Kickstarter's own tariff guidance says "someone has to pick up the tariff tab. It might be you, your manufacturer, or your backers" (https://updates.kickstarter.com/shipping-fulfillment-strategies-for-creators-facing-tariff-changes/). A 2026 analysis calls Tariff Manager "a collection tool, not a decision-making system" and warns that a surcharge added too early "can undercut the campaign's credibility" (https://blog.winsbs.com/2026/05/07/kickstarter-tariff-surcharges-board-games/). The cost of guessing wrong is large: 61% of funded projects ship late, French publisher FunForge absorbed roughly $250,000 of unexpected fulfillment costs on one campaign (https://updates.kickstarter.com/why-kickstarter-campaigns-fail-after-funding-and-how-to-avoid-it/), and Greater Than Games shut down blaming tariffs (https://www.tcf.team/blog/crowdfunding-in-2025). Creators pay for certainty.
first_30_days: Scrape live and recently funded tabletop and hardware campaigns whose updates mention "tariff" or "surcharge", and build a free public teardown of 20 of them (estimated landed cost vs price). Cold-email each creator their own teardown with an offer to run the real audit for $750. Partner with one customs broker for HTS review and one pledge-manager consultant for referrals. Close 5 paid audits and productise the recurring spreadsheet logic into a simple web form.

title: Escrowed Group Orders for Fandom Imports
one_liner: A group-order platform for K-pop, anime and idol merchandise that escrows money, consolidates freight under formal customs entry, and splits domestic shipping.
customer: Group-order managers (volunteer fans running orders on X, Instagram and Discord) and the fans who join their orders, plus small importers.
problem: US de minimis ended on 29 Aug 2025, so single parcels from Korea can be dutiable. Group orders run on PayPal Friends and Family and trust, and fraud is rife: Korea's police reported foreign-national fraud complaints rising from 5,307 (2023) to 19,907 (2025). Group-order managers personally carry the customs and refund risk.
solution: Managers list an order, participants pay into escrow, we purchase against verified receipts and aggregate into one commercial shipment (broker-filed entry, duties and product-safety rules handled), then split to US addresses with tracking. A reputation score for managers and automatic refunds when an order fails.
why_now: The de minimis change turned informal parcel-splitting into an importer-of-record problem, and scam volume is surging.
revenue_model: A 4-6% escrow fee, a freight and handling margin, and a manager subscription for tools.
non_obvious_insight: The informal fan trust economy has no importer and no escrow. Whoever becomes the compliant importer of record plus payment escrow captures the volume, because managers cannot solve duty on their own.
first_30_days: Partner with 5 mid-size US group-order managers. Run 3 orders end to end through a Korean freight forwarder. Charge the escrow fee and publish a public scam tracker for credibility.

title: Whisper Director for Immersive Theatre and LARP
one_liner: Beacon badges plus an AI conductor that whispers real-time cues to human actors so a 100-guest immersive show feels individually authored.
customer: Immersive theatre companies, escape-room chains, LARP organizers, corporate murder-mystery producers, and Meow Wolf-style venues.
problem: Immersive magic depends on actors responding to each guest, but no actor can track 100 people. Guests get generic loops, and shows stay small and unprofitable. Meow Wolf's Los Angeles and New York venues and Sphere's $420.5M gross show the demand.
solution: Version 1 is a stage-manager console. Guests wear BLE or UWB badges, software tracks paths and story flags, and an LLM plus rules engine produces cue whispers for performers via bone-conduction earpieces. There are no AI actors, only human performers with better information. Start with 40-person murder-mystery dinners and LARPs.
why_now: Low-latency LLMs and voice models, cheap beacons, and a live-experience boom make this feasible now, and the market is pushing toward permanent immersive venues.
revenue_model: $300-1,500 per production week, $5 per guest hardware rental, and licences for permanent installs.
non_obvious_insight: AI in entertainment is aimed at replacing performers, but the constrained resource in immersive theatre is coordination bandwidth, not talent. Human performers plus a conductor scales what audiences pay for.
first_30_days: Partner with 3 immersive producers or LARP groups. Rent BLE tags and run a 15-person cast pilot at a Halloween or winter event. Sell paid pilots at $2-4k per event.

title: Audit Desk for Indie Labels' AI-Remix Royalties
one_liner: Independent monitoring, consent management and statement auditing for the royalties that AI covers and remixes will start generating.
customer: Indie labels and publishers with 500-50,000 tracks, including Merlin, A2IM and IMPALA members, and their managers. Later, Merlin itself or collecting societies.
problem: Spotify and UMG will sell fan AI covers and remixes as a paid Premium add-on with 'consent, credit, compensation,' but no attribution method has been disclosed. Merlin joined on Aug 4, and Deezer's remix feature needs artist consent (Jun 24). Indie rights-holders will soon receive statement lines for derivative uses they cannot verify, across several programs with different opt-in rules.
solution: A dashboard that normalizes consent and pricing terms across programs (Spotify, Deezer, YouTube, licensed generators). An independent detector samples public remix and cover outputs using stem-level audio similarity to estimate each catalog's derivative usage. It reconciles the estimate against reported statements and prepares audit-rights letters when the numbers do not match. Delivered as a monthly report plus software.
why_now: The first major licensed-derivative programs launched in 2026, and Suno's Sep 9 move to a licensed-trained model shows a pay-for-use market forming. Indies have the least data and the weakest audit position.
revenue_model: $500-2,000/month per label, plus a contingency of 10-15% on recovered underpayments, which is standard for royalty audits, and an enterprise deal with an indie body.
non_obvious_insight: When a new royalty stream launches without a disclosed attribution method, the party with the least data needs an independent auditor. Royalty auditing is an established, profitable profession that no one has built for AI derivatives yet.
first_30_days: Take 10 indie labels through Merlin and A2IM contacts. Produce a free 'Derivative Exposure Report' scanning YouTube, TikTok and Deezer previews for AI covers of each label's top 50 tracks. Sell the monthly monitor, and recruit an advisor from a royalty-audit firm.

title: Cube Receipt: Win LTL Reclass and Reweigh Disputes
one_liner: A 45-second phone-based dimension-and-weight capture at the shipper's dock produces a timestamped, tamper-evident record attached to the BOL, then used to contest LTL carrier reclass and reweigh charges on contingency.
customer: Small and mid-size B2B shippers with $50K-$2M in annual LTL spend (furniture and home-goods makers, craft food and beverage, DTC brands shipping pallets, HVAC and parts distributors), plus small brokers who arrange LTL and absorb the adjustments when customers refuse to pay.
problem: The NMFC update on July 19, 2025 moved a large number of item numbers to density-based classification. Carriers reweigh and re-dimension freight at terminals with automated dimensioners and bill the corrected class, commonly a $30-$75 fee plus a 20-50% rate uplift. The shipper has no evidence of what actually left the dock, so the carrier's inspection is judge and jury. Most shippers just pay, and brokers who booked the load eat a share when the customer will not.
solution: A mobile app (iPhone LiDAR or camera) walks the packer through a pallet capture: dimensions with a reference marker, weight from a scale photo or entry, density and class check, wrap-bulge and overhang warnings, then hash and timestamp. It generates a QR sticker and a PDF appended to the BOL. When an adjustment invoice arrives (ingested from carrier emails or the freight audit feed), it auto-files the dispute with the evidence, tracks the carrier response, and takes a share of money recovered. It also flags pre-shipment problems, such as stretch-wrap bulge and pallet lip that inflate carrier-measured cube.
why_now: The July 2025 NMFC density shift is still generating adjustment invoices in 2026, and shippers are still learning the new classes. Phone LiDAR is ubiquitous, and carrier dimensioners are now the default at terminals, which makes source-side evidence the missing counterweight.
revenue_model: 25-30% of recovered adjustment charges (contingency), or $99-$299/month per dock. White-label to brokers at about $0.75 per shipment.
non_obvious_insight: Reclass is an evidence-asymmetry game, not a classification problem. The carrier's dimensioner records at the terminal and the shipper has nothing from the source. Terminal cube often includes bulging wrap and the pallet lip. A record made at tender time beats an after-the-fact photo inside the dispute window. Brokers see this daily in adjustment invoices but treat it as a cost of doing business rather than a product.
first_30_days: Approach 10 brokers who place LTL for small shippers. Each has adjustment invoices sitting in AR. Take six months of them, run manual disputes on contingency using whatever photos the shippers have, and log win rates by carrier. Build a no-code capture form (photo checklist plus timestamp) and put it on 3 shippers' docks. Use the win-rate data to sell the app.

title: Whey Capture Skids for Small Cheesemakers
one_liner: Leased containerized filtration skids that turn small cheese plants' cheap whey into sellable protein concentrate.
customer: Regional and farmstead cheese plants that sell whey for pennies or pay to dispose of it.
problem: Whey protein is scarce and pricey, yet small plants lack the ultrafiltration equipment and offtake to capture it, because equipment makers sell to giants.
solution: A leased, containerized ultrafiltration and diafiltration skid on revenue share, producing liquid whey protein concentrate that we sell to partner dryers and beverage makers.
why_now: Whey concentrate is up 108% in two years and isolate reaches $14/lb, so the byproduct now outearns its economics at small scale.
revenue_model: Skid lease plus a 30-40% revenue share on concentrate sold.
non_obvious_insight: The byproduct ate the product, and the largest untapped upside sits with small plants that big equipment vendors ignore.
first_30_days: Tour five plants in WI, VT and CA, quote a used UF skid, and pre-sell offtake to one beverage brand and one dryer.

title: Parametric Lease-Up Delay Insurance
one_liner: Insurance that pays automatically if a public submarket days-to-lease index stays high during a building's lease-up, protecting developers' interest carry.
customer: Multifamily developers and construction and mezzanine lenders with 100-400 unit buildings in lease-up (1.2M units nationally), sold through debt brokers.
problem: Lease-up interest carry balloons when time-to-lease stretches (34 days, longest September since 2019, with concessions on 15.8% of stabilized units). Lenders demand reserves or personal guarantees, sponsors self-insure, and traditional delay-in-start-up cover only addresses physical damage.
solution: A parametric policy that pays a pre-agreed sum if an index of median days-to-lease or vacancy exceeds a strike for N months in the lease-up window. Priced with an actuarial model, backed by reinsurer capacity, and sold as carry cover or a lender-accepted replacement for personal guarantees.
why_now: Lease-up glut and tight balance sheets create demand, parametric infrastructure (fronting carriers, index data, automated payouts) has matured, and starts are down 15.5%, so risk may be front-loaded.
revenue_model: 6-10% rate on line on $1-5M limits, plus MGA commission and profit share.
non_obvious_insight: Developers cannot influence a submarket's days-to-lease, so it is transparent and free of fraud, which makes it insurable. Capacity providers can view this as a defined macro bet with a supply-starts-driven mean reversion, though correlation across deals is the key risk.
first_30_days: Build an index from public rent and vacancy data. Quote 10 hypothetical developer and lender deals. Partner with a parametric MGA or coverholder for risk-carrying capacity and sign one $500K-limit pilot.

title: Shift-Matched Nurse Households Near Hospitals
one_liner: Master-lease three- and four-bedroom units near hospitals and match two single-parent nurses with interlocking shifts and similar-aged kids into one household, so overnight and early-morning care is built into the lease. The hospital pays for placement.
customer: Hospitals and health systems (per-placement or per-retained-nurse fee from recruitment and retention budgets), landlords in lease-up (guaranteed master-lease rent), and nurses (their half of rent).
problem: Single parents spend about 35% of income on childcare and the licensed system barely operates at night or on rotating schedules. Nurses' 12-hour rotating shifts do not fit center hours. Turnover of a bedside RN costs a hospital roughly $55-60K by industry surveys. Meanwhile large units near hospitals sit vacant behind concessions, and middle-income renters' late payments rose from 14.3% to 21.6% in a year.
solution: The platform (backed by the hospital's guarantee) master-leases large units from landlords for 12-24 months, then matches nurses on compatible shift patterns, school zone and child ages, with background checks, a shared household agreement, and an optional paid caregiver pool for overlap gaps. Each household pays about half the rent it would pay alone and has an adult at home when the other is at work. Students, residents and travel nurses can fill spare rooms.
why_now: Concessions of 15-37% and 7% vacancy make landlords eager for a guaranteed 12-24 month lease with a hospital-backed credit. Hospitals face the weakest cost position in years (Medicaid work requirements from Jan 2027 hit margins of expansion-state hospitals) and cannot afford travel-nurse premiums. Childcare costs are the top named barrier for early-career nurses.
revenue_model: Hospital fee per placed household (about $300-500 a month, justified by retention), plus a 10-15% spread on master-lease rent and caregiver-payroll fees.
non_obvious_insight: Matching on shift patterns is an algorithmic problem no housing platform solves: two nurses on opposite shifts convert the biggest cost in a household (childcare) into an internal schedule, and a hospital's guarantee turns a risky sublease into a credit-enhanced master lease that landlords will happily take at a discount.
first_30_days: Sign a pilot with one hospital's recruitment team and two landlords near campus. Master-lease two 3BR units and recruit four nurse parents from unit-level staffing forums. Write a household agreement and a safety-screening protocol with a family lawyer. Measure retention and shift coverage at 6 months.

title: Dumpster-Drop Leads for the Next Trade
one_liner: A white-label booking flow for independent roll-off dumpster companies that sells the homeowner's renovation start as an exclusive, unshared lead to the next trade in sequence.
customer: Local electricians, plumbers, drywall and paint, flooring and roofing shops pay per exclusive lead. Independent roll-off haulers (10-40 trucks) get revenue share and better booking software.
problem: 73% of homeowners have unstarted projects, 78% of them have no quotes, and the barriers are 'too busy' (21%), trust (21%) and no response (14%). Homeowner-plus-pro jobs rose from 27% to 46% while DIY-only fell from 50% to 39%. Angi charges $15-85 per lead and resells each to many bidders, and about 48% of home-service calls never reach a person.
solution: When a homeowner books a 10-30 yard bin, a two-question flow captures project type, timing, budget and lead-sharing consent. The hauler recommends one pre-vetted pro for the next step (electrical rough-in after demo, flooring after tear-out), with no bidding. The pro pays $50-120 only for an accepted lead. Drivers confirm project stage at swap-outs.
why_now: The DIY-plus-pro shift makes the demo-and-haul step the natural first purchase. Distrust of shared-lead marketplaces is high, and cheap AI text and voice booking lets small haulers add a lead flow without staff. Median home age is 44 years and remodeling spend hit a record $524B.
revenue_model: Per exclusive lead, about 40% shared with the hauler; SaaS for haulers at $99-299/mo; a recycled-C&D upsell.
non_obvious_insight: The dumpster is the earliest hard commitment in a remodel: money is spent and demo starts within days. The hauler is a locally trusted, neutral party that sees demand before any contractor quotes it. Its leads are exclusive, which is the opposite of Angi's economics.
first_30_days: Sign 3 independent haulers in one metro. Add consent and project questions to their web and phone booking. Recruit 6 pros (one per trade) at about $60 per exclusive lead. Measure booking-to-job conversion for a month and tune the trade sequence before adding metros.

title: Calibration Target Network for Earth-Observation Startups
one_liner: Networked ground calibration targets that issue overpass-synchronized calibration certificates for EO satellites.
customer: EO and SAR constellation operators, analytics firms selling certified measurements (insurance, methane, deforestation), and government agencies.
problem: Every new imaging satellite needs geometric and radiometric calibration, mostly done ad hoc. As EO output becomes regulated evidence, buyers ask who certified the sensor, and no third party provides traceable, on-demand ground truth.
solution: Deploy SAR corner reflectors, spectral tarps and instrumented sites (GPS, weather, irradiance) at a handful of stable locations. Automatically log each satellite overpass and issue a calibration certificate. Offer custom validation sites and controlled-release campaigns for customers.
why_now: The EO sector is mature and government-anchored (Planet's large contracts and Pelican production doubling per the briefing). Regulated uses raise demand for traceability. Many new SAR and hyperspectral entrants launch each year.
revenue_model: $30-150k per year per constellation. Project fees for custom validation sites. Certificates sold to analytics customers.
non_obvious_insight: As EO becomes evidence, the bottleneck is ground presence synchronized with overpasses, not more data.
first_30_days: Pick two well-known desert sites and place a first set of low-cost reflectors and tarps. Offer free certificates to three SAR and optical startups in return for testimonials, and ask for paid annual plans after the first quarter.

title: Clinician-Prescribed AI Social Practice for Kids
one_liner: A bounded, transcript-visible role-play partner that speech-language pathologists prescribe to autistic and socially anxious kids, sold to districts that are legally obliged to deliver therapy minutes.
customer: School-district special-education departments, contract therapy staffing firms (SLP, psychology) and private pediatric therapy clinics.
problem: Insiders think kids plus AI is a no-go zone. Character.AI barred under-18s from open-ended chat in November 2025, and the FTC 6(b) inquiry and state laws (CA SB 243) followed. But districts must deliver IEP speech and social-communication minutes, SLP caseloads are huge and vacancies persist. Kids need many low-stakes repetitions between weekly 30-minute sessions.
solution: An anti-companion design: the SLP assigns scripted scenarios (ordering lunch, joining a game, handling teasing). There is no persona, no persistent memory and no free topics. Practice is recorded and the SLP dashboard produces the progress-monitoring data IEPs require. Parents can read transcripts. Voice-first, tuned for child speech, with no audio retention by default.
why_now: Regulators and lawsuits (Raine v. OpenAI, Pennsylvania v. Character.AI) closed the open-ended companion door, which makes scoped, clinician-in-the-loop tools the defensible lane. Speech models handle child speech far better than they did two years ago. Special-ed budgets are stretched (from memory).
revenue_model: Per-student annual licence ($150-400), much cheaper than added SLP hours at $60-100 an hour. Clinics pay per clinician seat.
non_obvious_insight: The regulated lane isn't closed, it just has a different buyer: a clinician with a legal duty to document. Designing it as the opposite of a companion (no persona, no memory, no free chat) makes it compliant by construction and defensible in the next lawsuit.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 practicing SLPs to script 30 scenarios. Build a voice prototype. Run a 4-week paid pilot with about 10 kids in one private clinic ($99 a month per child). Then approach one contract-therapy staffing firm with the pilot's progress-monitoring data.

title: Notary-Witnessed Hiring Against Deepfake Candidates
one_liner: On-demand licensed notaries sit beside a remote candidate for the final interview or day-one onboarding and sign an attestation.
customer: Security and talent leads at remote-first software, fintech and defence-contractor employers, plus technical recruiting agencies, staffing firms and employer-of-record providers.
problem: An August 2026 eleven-nation advisory warned that North Korean IT-worker operations use real-time deepfakes to beat hiring checks, with 6,500+ similar cases reported globally. Employers face sanctions exposure. Liveness and document checks are being defeated, and the only alternatives are flying candidates in or trusting software.
solution: A marketplace and quality layer over existing mobile notaries and I-9 authorised representatives. A candidate books a witnessed final round in their own city. The witness checks ID, sweeps the room and desk for second screens and earpieces, positions a second camera, and signs a sealed attestation. An optional witnessed live-coding session runs on a locked, company-supplied laptop. A second 10-minute witnessed check at day 30 confirms identity continuity. Coverage starts in 200 US metros and expands to the UK and EU.
why_now: Real-time deepfake interviews are now mainstream and the 11-nation advisory (Aug 2026) is prompting boards to act. The DHS remote I-9 alternative procedure already blesses human 'authorised representatives'. Mobile signing agents lost volume when mortgage origination slumped, so witness supply is cheap.
revenue_model: $150-350 per witnessed session (about 60% to the witness), $2-10k per month enterprise subscriptions, and a per-hire fee for staffing agencies.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders think software has to beat deepfakes. For high-stakes moments, the cheapest defence is physics. A $200 human in the room costs less than one failed hire, and the scarce input is legally recognised people who already verify identity for a living. There are millions of commissioned US notaries.
first_30_days: Sign 40 notaries and loan-signing agents in five metros through signing-agent communities. Write a witness protocol and kit checklist, with legal review of what a notary may attest outside a notarial act. Pilot with three staffing firms or security-conscious startups.

title: Legal Defense Plan for Human-in-the-Loop Workers
one_liner: A USCCA-style membership that protects the nurse, safety driver or loan officer who gets blamed when AI recommends and a human signs, plus an 'override receipt' log the member personally owns.
customer: Unions, state nurses' associations and professional societies (radiologic technologists, CRNAs, claims adjusters, AV teleoperators and safety drivers) as distribution partners. Members pay through a dues add-on, or employers buy it as a retention benefit.
problem: Regulations and enterprise policies demand 'meaningful human oversight', which in practice makes the human the liability sponge, the 'moral crumple zone'. Uber's Tempe safety driver was criminally charged, and nurse RaDonda Vaught was convicted after overriding an automated dispensing cabinet. Employer indemnities and malpractice policies rarely cover AI-specific disputes, licensing-board action, or retaliation for raising concerns.
solution: (1) A prepaid legal defense retainer covering civil, licensing-board and criminal matters, with panel counsel experienced in tech-mediated harm. (2) 'Override receipts': a light app or extension where the member logs each override, disagreement or safety concern, with hashed timestamps in a member-owned escrow. (3) Plain-English 'working with this AI tool' duty briefings per workplace system. (4) Aggregated, anonymised incident data that gives unions leverage in bargaining over staffing and AI use.
why_now: AI decision support is now standard in hospitals (sepsis alerts, ambient scribes) and in robotaxi remote operations. Human-oversight duties are being written into the EU AI Act and state laws. Insurers' AI exclusions signal to employers that AI losses may be uninsured, so risk will be pushed down to individual workers. Unions are actively bargaining over AI in 2025-26.
revenue_model: $9-19 per member per month through associations, with margin after panel counsel and a reinsurer or legal-plan administrator. Employer-paid group plans and individual upsells.
non_obvious_insight: The person who actually absorbs AI risk is neither the deployer nor the vendor but the individual signer, and no product exists for them. Unions already have distribution and every reason to buy. The override-receipt record may be worth more than the defense cover, because it is the human-oversight evidence courts will look for, and it hands the union data on unsafe deployments.
first_30_days: Pick one narrow group, such as AV teleoperators and safety drivers or nurses in one state. Get an MOU with one union local or association. Retain a defense-firm panel at group rates. Ship the override log as a Chrome extension or SMS bot. Pre-sell 300 members at $12 per month, and check state prepaid-legal-plan rules first.

title: Cross-Mine Critical Spares Pool and Inventory Cleanup
one_liner: An AI cleaner for mine SAP materials masters that frees cash from duplicate spares, then turns the informal WhatsApp groups of competing mines' maintenance planners into a contractual, insured rotables pool for mill motors, liners and haul-truck parts.
customer: Supply chain, maintenance and finance heads at mid-size copper and lithium operations, starting in clusters where operators are neighbours: Arizona, Nevada and Utah, Antofagasta, the Arequipa-Moquegua corridor, the Zambian Copperbelt and the Pilbara. They pay a share of freed cash, not an IT budget.
problem: A copper mine holds $30-150M of spares. Materials masters are full of duplicates and near-duplicates (the same bearing under five descriptions), often 20-30% of items, so mines overbuy what is on another shelf. They still stock out on truly critical items (mill drive motors, girth gears, transformers, big castings) with 12-24 month lead times. Meanwhile maintenance planners across competing companies already borrow parts from each other over WhatsApp groups. It works only among friends and has no contracts, insurance, condition guarantees or return terms, so it never scales.
solution: Step one is the wedge. A CSV export of the SAP MM data goes into an LLM pipeline with OEM and aftermarket cross-references, multilingual description normalisation and criticality scoring. It outputs a list of duplicates, surplus and dead stock, plus the freed working capital in dollars. Step two lists surplus and 'insurance spares' on a members-only district board with a standard loan, lease and sale agreement, third-party condition inspection (vibration, NDT), logistics and insurance. It works like airline rotable pooling: three neighbouring mines share one spare mill motor instead of each stocking one.
why_now: Large motors, transformers and castings have longer lead times because of grid and data-centre demand. Steel and copper tariffs make replacement parts pricier. Lithium mines are cash-starved after the price bust, and copper mines face cost inflation and grade decline, so CFOs are hunting working capital. LLMs can now normalise messy multilingual part descriptions at almost no cost, which was not economic three years ago.
revenue_model: 15-25% of freed cash (sales and avoided purchases only, not write-offs), a pool membership subscription ($1-3k per month), and an 8-10% transaction fee on pooled loans and sales, plus inspection and certification fees.
non_obvious_insight: The spares problem is legal and trust-based, not a software problem. The informal swap network is the real supply chain. The biggest saving is not selling dead stock, it is not buying the 'insurance spare' a neighbour already owns. Pooling is an aviation idea that mining has never adopted because competitors will not share data without a neutral third party.
first_30_days: Through ex-colleagues, offer a free 2-week scan of SAP MM exports (CSV) at two or three mid-size mines. Deliver a dollar value of duplicates and surplus and a target list. Sign a success-fee agreement with the first one that shows a big number. In parallel, seed a private 'list before you buy' board among 20 maintenance planners in one district using Signal or WhatsApp, to formalise the network before any software is built.

title: Workout GC for Stalled Spec Homes
one_liner: A finish-the-house crew and re-sequencing service sold to construction lenders, not builders, for homes stuck at 40-90% complete.
customer: Community banks, credit unions and private construction lenders with spec-home loans being extended (Texas, Florida, Southeast, Mountain West). Secondary customer: distressed small builders referred by those lenders.
problem: Starts hold at 1.275M SAAR but completions fell 27.1% YoY. One executive described 15-20 houses stuck on foundations for 6+ weeks, and a West Virginia builder risks about 40 closings. The builder cannot get crews back, and the lender holds the real risk: exhausted interest reserves, mechanic's liens, extensions, and half-built collateral. Lenders have no operating arm.
solution: Start with a flat-fee stuck-loan triage: site visit, photo scan, cost-to-finish, days of carry and sub availability, ranked across the lender's watchlist. Then take over scheduling and finishing on cost-plus. A few in-house supers plus a pre-vetted bench of framing, MEP and finish subs are paid in 7 days through the lender's normal draw process. The builder keeps the lot and the sale. A bonus is paid per day saved before the extension deadline.
why_now: Completions are down 27.1% while starts hold. 63% of builders already use incentives and 35% cut prices, so there is no margin left to absorb delay. ICE arrests rose from 32,545 in May to 49,571 in July 2026 and are pulling crews off sites. 2027 starts are forecast down 2-4%, so more small builders will stall. The 2024-25 vintage of spec construction loans is maturing now.
revenue_model: $2.5K per-loan triage or $15K portfolio review. Finishing work at cost plus 12-15%. Success fee of about 1% of loan balance for closing before the extension deadline.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone frames stalled homes as a builder or labor problem. The party with the budget, the legal leverage and no ego is the lender, who cares about loan resolution rather than building. Subs return when someone credible promises six straight days of work and pays in a week. A lender-backed GC has that payment credibility and the stalled builder does not.
first_30_days: Call 15 construction lenders and workout officers through state bankers associations. Offer two banks a free 10-loan triage. Hire two ex-superintendents. Line up 3 framing, MEP and finish subs per metro on a 7-day-pay promise. Target a first paid contract on 1-3 homes by day 30.

title: Heat and Smoke Stop-Day Kit for Outdoor Crews
one_liner: Text-message heat and smoke compliance for small outdoor employers, sold through comp carriers and PEOs, with parametric stop-day cover to follow.
customer: Workers' comp carriers and PEOs serving small landscapers, roofers, framers and farms in California, Washington and Oregon (later AZ, TX, CO), plus general contractors that need subs' plans.
problem: OSHA's federal heat rule has slipped (supplemental proposal Dec 2026, final Oct 2027), but California, Washington and Oregon already bind employers. Small crews have no written plan, acclimatization tracking or go/no-go rule. Heat and smoke stop-work days hurt small-contractor cash flow, and business-interruption cover for them is barely productized.
solution: Phase one is a text-message-first kit: site-level heat and air-quality alerts, a state-specific written plan, water, shade and break logs, acclimatization schedules and audit exports. Phase two adds parametric stop-day cover through an MGA partner, with WBGT or AQI triggers.
why_now: The summer 2026 shock and state rules make compliance urgent, while federal delay pushes pressure onto carriers and GCs.
revenue_model: $39-99 per crew per month, or per-employee fees from carriers and PEOs for loss control, plus parametric premium margin later.
non_obvious_insight: Demand does not depend on OSHA. States, general-contractor prequalification and comp-carrier loss control drive it.
first_30_days: Pitch two comp-carrier loss-control teams and a landscaping association. Run a 20-crew pilot with the plan generator and alerts.

title: Fraud-Proof Sourcing for the Dye-and-Whey Scramble
one_liner: A concierge service that authenticates certificates of analysis, brokers and supplier identities for supply-short ingredients such as natural colors and whey.
customer: Procurement and QA or regulatory teams at $50M-3B food, beverage and private-label manufacturers reformulating away from petroleum dyes (Walmart private label dye-free in Jan 2027, FDA target Dec 2027) or scrambling for whey.
problem: Natural colorant demand is projected to rise 400-500%, the US is 98% import-dependent for annatto, and reformulation costs $50K-500K per SKU over 12-24+ months. Whey concentrate is up 108% in two years and some suppliers are sold out through 2026. Shortages under deadline pressure bring new brokers, prepayment demands and adulteration risk. Generative AI makes certificates of analysis, lab letterheads and audit certificates trivial to forge, and QA teams verify by email.
solution: For each lot: a direct callback or API check with the issuing lab (signed lab-issued COAs where possible), document forensics (metadata, accreditation numbers versus registries), supplier identity and beneficial-owner checks, bank-account-name match to catch payment redirection, and importer-chain (FSVP) checks. Members contribute data to a pooled adulteration signature library (chromatography and spectral patterns) that becomes the moat.
why_now: Two hard deadlines (Walmart Jan 2027, FDA Dec 2027) and a whey shortage are forcing buyers to source from unfamiliar suppliers now. More than 70 alt-protein companies have folded or been acquired since September 2024, so distressed ingredient stock is moving through brokers. Forging documents with AI is now near-free.
revenue_model: $250-600 per verified lot on a concierge basis, then $2-6K a month subscriptions for monitoring and access to the member data pool, plus lab referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: In shortages the fraudster's edge is paperwork, not chemistry. Buyers under deadline pressure waive diligence. A KYC layer that never touches a molecule but is bonded to accredited labs can become the trust network, and the pooled fingerprint library gets more valuable with every member.
first_30_days: Reach 10 QA directors on LinkedIn. Offer the first 5 COA verifications free in exchange for lot data. Sign 2 accredited labs for callback verification. Publish a one-page 'natural color and whey counterfeits to watch' guide for lead generation. Convert 3 pilots at about $2,500 each.

title: Menu Trial Lab: Restaurants as Food-Brand Test Sites
one_liner: A network of two-to-five-unit restaurants that run randomized menu experiments for food brands and commodity boards, and get paid for it.
customer: Emerging food and beverage brands (sauces, blended or alternative proteins, beverages), commodity checkoff boards (beef, pork, dairy, potato, avocado and similar), and distributor private-label teams pay $10-25k per trial. Independent operators are paid a fee and free product and get menu-engineering results back.
problem: Foodservice launches fail because the operator's ROI is unproven, not because guests dislike the item. Line speed, storage, training, plate cost and cannibalization decide whether an item survives. Brands pay for sales reps, menu-placement deals and consumer surveys, but survey data measures stated preference. The item then sits in my walk-in. Reps tell operators 'it sells' with no data to prove it.
solution: Recruit a network of 2-5-unit independents who connect Toast, Square or Clover. Each trial is a randomized matched-pair test: the item is on the menu at one location and not at its twin, then swapped, and we run a difference-in-differences on attach rate, check average, cannibalization, plate cost and contribution margin per cover. The deliverable is a 'Menu Adoption Scorecard' plus an operator-facing ROI one-pager the brand's reps and distributors can use to close accounts. Automated matched-pair design and automated POS reading keep unit costs low.
why_now: Beef, coffee, cocoa and dairy cost pressure has kept operators reformulating (blends, substitutions) since 2025, and brands need proof under tighter budgets. POS platform APIs and partner ecosystems now make continuous read access practical at scale. AI makes experiment design and reporting cheap. Commodity boards and distributors are under pressure to show operator-level ROI. I could not verify whether an existing network already sells this, so check Datassential, Technomic and distributor pilot programs first.
revenue_model: Fee per trial ($10-25k) paid by the brand or board, with a portion (say $500-2,000) paid to each participating operator. Later, annual data subscriptions for brand teams and 'scorecard' licensing to distributors.
non_obvious_insight: A two-location owner is a natural experimenter, since it is the only cheap way to run a true A/B with identical kitchens, menus and staff. Nobody in food innovation uses that. The buyer's real question is 'will an operator make money and keep it on the menu', which no consumer panel answers. The moat is the operator network and their POS data, not the analytics.
first_30_days: Post in owner Facebook groups and a regional restaurant association to recruit 10 two-to-five-unit operators, including my own two locations as pilot sites. Approach 5 emerging brands at a regional foodservice show with a $5-8k, four-week matched-pair trial. Run my first trial in my own two restaurants and turn the results into a 3-page scorecard to use as the sales collateral for the next brand.

title: Hatchery-Specific Phage Cocktails on Subscription
one_liner: A monthly service that isolates each shrimp hatchery's own Vibrio strains and ships a custom bacteriophage cocktail to kill them, so hatcheries can stop using antibiotics.
customer: Shrimp hatcheries and nurseries in Vietnam, India, Ecuador and Indonesia, plus the exporters and feed companies that buy their post-larvae and need antibiotic-free supply.
problem: Vibrio outbreaks (AHPND/EMS) wipe out whole hatchery batches. Antibiotics are banned in export markets, but residues keep turning up: a 2025 analysis attributes 43% of shrimp export rejections by the EU, US and Japan to chloramphenicol and nitrofuran residues, and 19 Indian consignments were rejected in 2025-26. Post-larvae pass through fragmented hatcheries and aggregators, so nobody can trace or fix the source. Generic probiotics and disinfectants work unevenly.
solution: A lab-in-a-box subscription. We sample water and biofilm each month and sequence and culture the local Vibrio isolates. We screen them against a curated phage library and ship a hatchery-specific cocktail as a water or feed additive. The cocktail is refreshed as strains drift, and later we add AI-designed phages. Each shipment comes with a residue-free 'clean seed' data pack that exporters and buyers can audit. Selling it in the feed-additive or probiotic regulatory class, not as a drug, keeps approval fast in most shrimp-producing countries.
why_now: Antibiotic bans (India's March 2025 notification banning chloramphenicol and nitrofurans in food-producing animals) are colliding with continued export rejections. Generative phage design became real in September 2025, when the Arc Institute and Stanford, using the Evo genome models, produced 16 viable AI-designed phage genomes from 302 candidates, later published in Science. Nanopore sequencing is cheap enough to run near ponds. Buyers now demand antibiotic-free attestations.
revenue_model: Subscription of roughly $400-1,500 per month per hatchery, scaled by tank volume, plus per-batch emergency cocktails at a premium. Exporters or feed companies pay a per-lot attestation fee. Longer term, license the phage library and drift dataset to feed and biosecurity companies.
non_obvious_insight: A phage is host-specific and keeps evolving with its target, so it works badly as a mass-market molecule and well as a perishable, local, continuously updated service. Big pharma cannot profitably do bespoke, and that is the wedge. The moat is the living library of regional strains and the resistance-drift dataset, and the hatchery is the chokepoint of the whole seed supply chain, so clean seed pays off downstream.
first_30_days: Partner with one university phage lab in Vietnam, India or Ecuador. Offer 10 hatcheries free strain-isolation reports to build the initial library, and pitch each hatchery a $500-per-month paid pilot. Ask one export processor to sponsor 3 pilots to secure antibiotic-free seed for its supply chain.

title: Marginalia: Lived-Experience Annotated Books
one_liner: One-of-one physical books annotated in ink by people who have actually lived what the book is about, such as a retired ER nurse in The Plague or a lighthouse keeper's daughter in To the Lighthouse.
customer: Gift buyers and collectors paying $250-1,200 per copy, quarterly-subscription readers ($180/quarter), independent bookstores, libraries and special collections, and professional associations gifting to retirees.
problem: Explanations and summaries are free and infinite, so 'I've read it' signals nothing. Celebrity-signed copies signal fame, not thought. What is scarce is a particular lived mind reading a text in real time: dated, physical, opinionated, and accountable.
solution: Recruit about 100 'readers of record': retired judges, surgeons, sommeliers, deep-sea divers, and translators. Match each to a canonical book that fits their life. Each annotates a physical copy under a fixed protocol: at least 60 marginal notes, a two-page flyleaf letter, a signed colophon, and a one-take authenticity video. Copies are numbered and sold. A commission tier lets you order a book annotated by someone in your recipient's own profession (a retirement gift for a fire chief). Displaced translators can annotate a translation against the original, showing what the machine misses.
why_now: AI summarizers have made shallow reading free, so deep, lived reading is the differentiator. The 2026 human-made premium is well documented. Physical-book culture is holding up, and the 'association copy' idea is old and understood among collectors.
revenue_model: Per-copy sales (reader 40%, platform about 45%, materials about 15%), a quarterly subscription, institutional acquisitions, and annual charity auctions of 'famous minds' copies.
non_obvious_insight: In an age of infinite explanation, the scarce good is witnessed subjectivity. A marginal note is a physical, un-averaged opinion, the opposite of what a language model produces. Collectors already pay premiums for association copies (a book owned or annotated by someone notable). This manufactures them prospectively and at scale.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 readers through retirement communities and professional associations. Produce 30 copies. Sell through a Substack with page photos and pre-orders. Approach 5 indie bookstores for consignment. Goal: $10k in pre-orders by day 60.

title: Delay-Suit Rails for Stuck Immigration Cases
one_liner: White-label filing infrastructure that lets solo immigration lawyers file mandamus/APA delay lawsuits in 48 hours, turning the government's habit of mooting suits into a flat-fee product.
customer: Solo and small immigration firms (1-10 attorneys) who pay a per-filing platform fee; end clients (naturalization, green card and employment petition applicants) pay the firm a flat $2.5-5k. Secondary buyer: employers with stuck petitions.
problem: Cases are stuck well past posted processing times: interviewed N-400s never scheduled for oath, I-485s and I-140s idling, and holds or pauses applied to nationals of dozens of countries since late 2025. Clients wait 12-30 months. Lawyers know a federal delay suit often shakes a case loose, but most solos have never filed one. Drafting the complaint, civil cover sheet, summons, service on the U.S. Attorney's civil process clerk, the Attorney General and the agency, and district-specific local rules is a 6-10 hour learning curve, and no one wants to be the first to file.
solution: A web tool with three parts. (1) An eligibility screen: enter the receipt date, form type and field office, and it compares them to posted times and to real observed outcomes, then scores the delay claim. (2) A complaint and exhibit generator with a per-district rules library, a service-of-process checklist and deadline calendar (the 60-day government answer window), and a template for the joint status report or stipulated dismissal that follows adjudication. (3) A docket-outcome database that logs, by district, judge and case type, how long from filing to adjudication. The attorney of record signs every filing. The platform is software, not a law firm.
why_now: Through late 2025 and 2026 USCIS added enhanced vetting, holds and pauses on benefit requests tied to nationality, expanded re-review of approved cases, and slower naturalization and green card scheduling. The volume of genuinely stuck cases is at a decade high. Federal courts are also less deferential to agencies since the Loper Bright decision, and adjudicating a stuck case is cheaper for the government than defending it. Solos are overloaded and short of billable-hour alternatives, so a ready-made product for a high-ticket service is easy to sell.
revenue_model: $350-600 per filing charged to the law firm (flat, not a percentage, to avoid fee-splitting rules), or $299/month for up to 3 filings. Later: a paid intelligence tier of docket-outcome analytics by district, and a litigation-funding partnership for clients who can't front the fee.
non_obvious_insight: The lawsuit is rarely litigated to judgment. The U.S. Attorney's Office usually tells USCIS to adjudicate within 30-90 days so the suit can be dismissed as moot, so the client's real purchase is a forced deadline. Clients almost never hear about this because form-prep firms earn on the application, not on pressure. Posted processing times are also misleading (they reflect only completed cases at a percentile), so whoever accumulates real time-to-decision data by field office and district owns the moat.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 immigration attorneys in high-volume districts (N.D. Cal., S.D. Tex., D.N.J., E.D.N.Y., S.D. Fla.) and offer free templates for the first filing. Build the intake screen and three complaint templates first (delayed N-400 after interview, delayed I-485, delayed I-130/I-140 or a nationality hold). Concierge-run 10 filings by hand, charging the firms $400 each. Log every outcome date, since that dataset is the product. Post outcome stats to immigration-lawyer Facebook groups and AILA chapter listservs to pull in the next 30 firms.

title: Snow Mutual: Weather Swaps Between Opposite Businesses
one_liner: A peer-to-peer weather-swap exchange that nets opposite snowfall exposures inside a metro, matching per-push plow operators with seasonal-flat operators and per-push property managers so no one pays insurer-grade premiums.
customer: Independent snow-plow and landscaping contractors (10-200 trucks) and small commercial property managers, HOAs and retail owners in Great Lakes and Northeast snowbelts.
problem: Snow contracts are weather bets. A dry winter crushes per-push operators' revenue while truck notes, insurance and retainer labor stay fixed. A heavy winter blows up seasonal-flat operators' costs and property managers' per-push budgets. Traditional insurance for this is thin and expensive, so nearly everyone is unhedged.
solution: Standardized index contracts, either seasonal snowfall or count of 2+ inch events at a named NWS/airport station. They are matched inside a metro. The platform holds collateral, nets opposing positions and lays off only the residual to a reinsurer or weather-derivative desk. Onboarding asks for your contract mix and returns a 'snow exposure score' and a suggested swap. Version one is an index-linked price-collar clause in the service contract itself, which needs no insurance license. A licensed MGA structure follows.
why_now: NOAA CPC/IRI's September 2026 outlooks put a greater than 90% chance on a very strong El Niño this winter, and seasonal snowfall maps lean below normal for the Great Lakes and Northeast, with lake-effect still a wildcard. Sentiment is lopsided and uncertain. Renewals and pricing decisions happen between now and November, so contractors are actively thinking about winter risk.
revenue_model: A fee of 8-12% of matched notional, charged to both sides, plus a small annual membership. Later, a margin on the unmatched residual layer and reinsurance placement fees.
non_obvious_insight: The snow industry already contains natural hedgers on both sides of every winter. Operators with per-push books and operators with seasonal-flat books have opposite exposures, and so do property managers. The need is mostly a matching problem, and matching removes the capital cost that makes small-business weather cover uneconomic.
first_30_days: Recruit through snow-industry associations, plow-forum groups and property-management associations. Sign about 15 operators and 15 property managers in one metro. Draft the index-collar addendum with a commercial lawyer and run a pilot on winter 2026-27 contracts with small capped notionals. Line up an MGA and a reinsurance quote for the residual.
